(frog-nbo)=
# frog-nbo

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-primary}`Parsing` Extract Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) data from ORCA output (! NBO).

## What it does

NBO (Natural Bond Orbital) analysis rewrites the wavefunction as a Lewis structure: core orbitals
(CR), lone pairs (LP), bonds (BD) and their empty counterparts (antibonds BD*, Rydberg RY). It
answers chemists' questions directly: **NPA charges** (natural population analysis, much less
basis-set dependent than Mulliken), hybridisation of a bond (sp², % s character), **Wiberg bond
indices** (bond orders) and the **E(2) donor→acceptor energies** that quantify hyperconjugation
and delocalisation (e.g. n(O) → σ*(C–X), anomeric effects, π conjugation). The NBO output is
thousands of lines long; this command extracts the parts you need, filtered by atom, and can
turn selected NBOs into cube files to look at.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-nbo/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

An **ORCA output with an NBO analysis**: add `! NBO` to the input (ORCA 5/6 with the NBO 7
program installed and the `NBOEXE` environment variable set). NPA charges, the NBO list and the
E(2) table are printed by default. **Wiberg bond indices** need an extra keyword:
`%nbo NBOKEYLIST = "$NBO BNDIDX $END" end`. A **Gaussian log** with `pop=nbo` (Gaussian's
NBO 3.1) works too: NPA charges, the NBO list with occupancies and energies and the E(2) table
are checked against an ORCA twin (Wiberg indices from Gaussian are not checked). NBO 3.1 numbers
the NBOs in a different order than NBO 7 and calls the Rydbergs `RY*`, so compare the two
programs by label (`LP ( 2) O 1`), not by NBO number; E(2) values involving Rydbergs differ by
a few tenths of a kcal/mol between the two NBO versions.

For `--cube`/`--cube-e2` the output must also contain the basis set: ORCA `! PrintBasis
PrintMOs`; Gaussian `#p ... pop=(full,nbo) iop(3/33=1) iop(6/80=1) gfinput`. The NBO
coefficients are read from the `.37` file written by the NBO `PLOT` keyword
(`%nbo NBOKEYLIST = "$NBO PLOT $END" end`; give it with `--coeff-file` if it is not next to the
output); without it they are rebuilt from the hybrids printed in the output, which covers
core, lone-pair, bond and antibond NBOs only.

Numbering: atom indices (`-i`) are **0-based** (first atom = 0), while the labels printed by NBO
(e.g. `O 17`) and the NBO numbers (`--cube 44`) are **1-based**, as in the NBO output.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | ORCA output files with an NBO analysis (! NBO) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` |  | Show the full analysis (summary, NPA, NBOs, E(2), Wiberg; bonds and lone pairs with -i) |
| `--summary` |  | Show a short summary of the NBO analysis |
| `--npa` |  | Show NPA charges |
| `--analysis` |  | Show the NBO list (occupancy, energy, hybrid composition) |
| `--e2` |  | Show second-order E(2) perturbation energies |
| `--wiberg` |  | Show the Wiberg bond index matrix and atom totals |
| `--bonds` |  | Show bond orbitals (BD) of the selected atoms (first two of -i) |
| `--lp` |  | Show lone pair orbitals (LP) of the selected atom (first of -i) |
| `--cycle` `CYCLE` | `-1` | NBO cycle to inspect (-1 = last/converged, 0 = first) |
| `-i`, `--indices` `INDICES …` |  | Keep only results involving any of these atoms (0-based) |
| `--dtype` `DTYPE` |  | Filter E(2) by donor type (e.g. LP, BD) |
| `--atype` `ATYPE` |  | Filter E(2) by acceptor type (e.g. BD*, RY) |
| `--cube` `N …` |  | Write cube files of these NBOs (1-based NBO numbers) |
| `--cube-e2` `[K]` |  | Write cube files of the donor and acceptor NBOs of the K strongest E(2) interactions (K = 3 if omitted) |
| `--coeff-file` `PATH` |  | NBO coefficient file (.37, from the NBO PLOT keyword); auto-detected next to the input if omitted |
| `--spacing` `SPACING` | `0.15` | Grid spacing in Å |
| `--voxels` `VOXELS` |  | Number of grid points per axis (overrides --spacing) |
| `--padding` `PADDING` | `5.0` | Box padding around the molecule in Å |

**Thresholds**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-t`, `--threshold` `THRESHOLD` | `2.0` | E(2) threshold in kcal/mol |

**Ensemble averaging**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-c`, `--checkpoint` `PATH` |  | Checkpoint file (checkpoint.json, or csv/json) with Boltzmann populations for ensemble averaging |
| `--read-boltzmann` `PROTOCOL` |  | Protocol whose populations are read from the checkpoint (default: protocol of each file, or the latest) |
| `-e`, `--energy-term` `{E,EZPVE,H,G}` | `G` | Energy used for on-the-fly Boltzmann weights |
| `-T`, `--temp` `TEMP` | `298.15` | Temperature in K |
| `--individual` |  | Also show per-conformer results next to the ensemble average |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for the <stem>_nbo_cubes/ folders (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `Natural Population Summary (<file>)` | `--summary/--all` | Total, Lewis and non-Lewis populations |
| Terminal | `NPA Charge Extremes (<file>)` | `--summary/--all` | Three most positive and most negative NPA charges (e) |
| Terminal | `Top 5 E(2) Interactions (<file>)` | `--summary/--all` | Strongest donor-acceptor interactions (kcal/mol) |
| Terminal | `NPA Charges (<file>)` | `--npa` | One row per atom: natural charge, valence and Rydberg population |
| Terminal | `Natural Bond Orbital Analysis (<file>)` | `--analysis` | One row per NBO: type, atoms, occupancy, energy (au) and hybrid composition |
| Terminal | `NBO Bonds (<file>)` | `--bonds` | Bond orbitals (BD/BD*) of the selected atoms |
| Terminal | `NBO Lone Pairs (<file>)` | `--lp` | Lone pairs (LP) of the selected atom |
| Terminal | `Wiberg Bond Index Matrix (<file>)` | `--wiberg` | Atom x atom Wiberg bond indices |
| Terminal | `Wiberg Totals (<file>)` | `--wiberg` | Total Wiberg valence of each atom |
| Terminal | `Detailed Interactions (> <t> kcal/mol) (<file>)` | `--e2` | Donor-acceptor pairs with E(2) above -t (kcal/mol) and ΔE (au) |
| Terminal | `Aggregated Interactions (Sum > <t> kcal/mol) (<file>)` | `--e2` | E(2) summed over equivalent donor-acceptor pairs |
| Terminal | `NBO Cubes (<file>)` | `--cube/--cube-e2` | One row per cube: NBO, type, label, occupancy, energy and path |
| Terminal | `Ensemble Weights (<n> conformers)` | `-c` | Conformer, protocol, file, Boltzmann population (%) and normalized weight (%) |
| Terminal | `Ensemble-Averaged NPA Charges / Wiberg / E(2) Interactions` | `-c` | Boltzmann-weighted versions of the --npa, --wiberg and --e2 tables |
| File | `<stem>_nbo_cubes/<stem>_nbo<N>_<label>.cube` | `--cube/--cube-e2` | NBO N on a grid (E(2) pairs: <stem>_e2p<k>_donor\|acceptor_nbo<N>_<label>.cube) |
| File | `<stem>_nbo_cubes/view_chimerax.cxc, view_pymol.pml` | `--cube/--cube-e2` | ChimeraX and PyMOL scripts that open all cubes of the input |

### How to read it

Tables in the terminal, one block per file. Units: charges in e, occupancies in electrons,
E(2) in kcal/mol, orbital energies and ΔE (donor–acceptor energy gap) in Hartree (au).

* **Lewis population** of a well-described closed-shell organic molecule is ≥ 97–98 % of the
  electrons; a much lower value means strong delocalisation (or that one Lewis structure is a
  poor description, e.g. in some metal complexes).
* Bond orbital occupancies are close to 2.0 (e.g. 1.96), antibonds close to 0 (0.02–0.1);
  a BD* with ≥ 0.3 e is strongly populated by hyperconjugation.
* E(2) above ~5 kcal/mol is a significant interaction, above ~20 kcal/mol a strong one
  (typical for n → σ*/π* in conjugated or anionic systems). The *Aggregated* table sums
  E(2) over the separate entries NBO prints for the same donor/acceptor pair (e.g. two lone pairs
  of the same oxygen).
* An optimisation with `! Opt NBO` prints one NBO analysis per cycle in ORCA: the **last** one
  (`--cycle -1`, default) belongs to the final geometry.
* "No Wiberg bond index matrix found" means the `BNDIDX` keyword was not in the input.
* Known limitations: with ORCA/NBO 7 outputs the **E (au)** column of `--analysis`, `--bonds` and
  `--lp` currently shows 0.0000 (the energies are in the NBO summary of the output), and the
  *Hybrid Composition* lists only the first atom of a two-centre bond.

Example (`nbo.out`, a 37-atom anion C16H13BrF3O3S⁻, B3LYP/def2-TZVP): 211.9999 electrons, Lewis
97.88 %, 845 NBOs; most positive NPA charge S15 (NBO label; FROG index 14) +2.048, most negative O18 −0.942; strongest E(2)
LP O 17 → BD* S 15–C 19, 26.48 kcal/mol (ΔE 0.33 au), BD* S 15–C 19 occupancy 0.35.

## Step by step

1. Get an overview first: `frog-nbo job.out --summary` (Lewis/non-Lewis population, most positive/negative NPA charges, five strongest E(2) interactions).
2. Ask for the sections you need: `--npa` (charges), `--analysis` (all NBOs with occupancy and hybrids), `--e2` (donor→acceptor energies), `--wiberg`, or `--all` for everything.
3. Focus on a site with `-i` (0-based atoms): `--e2 -i 16 --dtype LP -t 5` keeps only lone-pair donations involving atom 16 above 5 kcal/mol; `--bonds -i 14 18` shows the bond orbitals between atoms 14 and 18, `--lp -i 16` the lone pairs of atom 16.
4. Visualise orbitals: `--cube-e2 3` writes the donor and acceptor NBOs of the 3 strongest E(2) interactions, `--cube 44 144` specific NBOs, into `<stem>_nbo_cubes/` together with ChimeraX (`view_chimerax.cxc`) and PyMOL (`view_pymol.pml`) scripts; use `--voxels 60` for a quick test.
5. For a conformer ensemble add `-c checkpoint.json` to Boltzmann-average NPA charges, Wiberg indices and E(2) values.

                file [file ...]

Extract Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) data from ORCA output (! NBO).

Prints NPA charges, NBO occupancies and compositions, bonds, lone pairs, Wiberg bond indices and
second-order E(2) donor-acceptor energies, and builds cube files of selected NBOs. NBO numbers
(--cube) are 1-based as in the NBO output; atom indices (-i) are 0-based.
